reviews.text: Lulu Wang has made an expertly and sagely constructed ode to both western and eastern values, joining them together with familial sentimentality, resulting in charm and effortless poignancy.
reviews.author: Calum Cooper

reviews.text: The Farwell is not only a loving tribute to the women who carry our families, but it’s deeply relatable, with humor and honesty shining through the somber moments of life.
reviews.author: Ryan McQuade

reviews.text: In this powerful family drama, Awkwafina's performance transcends culture and dares you not to cry.
reviews.author: Elisa Guimarães

reviews.text: A worthwhile diversion to so much summer blockbuster fare.
reviews.author: Greg Carlson

reviews.text: An opening title card tells us this is a film “Based on an actual lie.” Funny thing is “The Farewell” is one of the truest movies about illness and grief I’ve seen in a while.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Lulu Wang’s The Farewell is a groundbreaking work that’s authentic and deeply affecting.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: The upcoming death feels like a metaphor for the movie itself. It brings some universal theme around family and immigration, but it's just way, way too slow. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Victor Pineyro

reviews.text: The Farewell is heartwarming, capably made, exceptionally well-acted, and achingly sincere without ever resorting to sentimentality.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Episode 45: The Farewell / Jackie Brown / Once Upon a Time... in Hollywood
reviews.author: Taylor Baker

reviews.text: Bring a box of tissues... [Awkwafina] is super darling.
reviews.author: Lonita Cook

reviews.text: Lulu Wang's The Farewell is a particularly articulate piece of filmmaking. It beautifully captures the sense of alienation of a child of two cultures, and finds warmth and humour in little family moments.
reviews.author: Maria Lattila

reviews.text: Lulu Wang's The Farewell is bittersweet in the truest sense of the word, balancing on the knife edge of grief and joy.
reviews.author: Yasmin Omar

reviews.text: The movie wants you to believe that there are no easy answers [...] But unfortunately, there are easy answers here, and The Farewell did not do a good enough job of convincing me that this lie was necessary or ethical.
reviews.author: Cate Young

reviews.text: No matter where you come from, you'll likely find some point of connection with The Farewell. The film's themes of love and loss resonate far beyond its Chinese location, thanks to a talented cast and deft writing and directing.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: Isn't this life? Nobody really knows, we just do the best we can.
reviews.author: Fletcher Powell

reviews.text: It is remarkable that Wang created this film...steeped in Chinese and Chinese-American culture and yet has a message so strong that it can appeal to wide audiences.
reviews.author: Nicole Ackman

reviews.text: A slow burn, a movie that builds to a poignant climax that not only feels earned but deserved.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: A profound meditation on young vs. old and East vs. West, [The Farewell] looks to bridge a generational and cultural divide...through reconciliation and understanding.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Zhang

reviews.text: It is exactly what it is, unapologetically. A funny, sweet, heart-felt, heart-wrenching film about family, identity, love and loss.
reviews.author: Candice McMillan

reviews.text: Such an average, uneventful, small, intimately-designed, down-to-earth, slice-of-life drama that very little of it is memorable.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: The fact it's based on writer-director Lulu Wang's real life experiences only adds the poignancy.
reviews.author: Charlotte Harrison

reviews.text: As authentic and involving as a family drama could hope to be, and one of the most effective takes on the tension between culture and identity seen in the last few years
reviews.author: James Mudge

reviews.text: The Farewell packs a powerful emotional punch while still offering plenty of humor to give it some levity.
reviews.author: Matthew St. Clair

reviews.text: Wang has produced an utter marvel of a film. The Farewell is a beautiful, resonating gem, fuelled by some standout performances and told with touches of pure grace.
reviews.author: James Hanton

reviews.text: It's about watching, about waiting. It's when it's at its most natural that The Farewell connects the inside and the outside with an honesty that's hard to resist.
reviews.author: Matt Cipolla

reviews.text: The second film as director of Lulu Wang doesn't move me nor does it seem funny, but I can't deny that it contains a certain intimacy with the intercultural treaty that describes the vicissitudes of a Chinese family. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: "The Farewell" will fill you with the same feeling as Yasujirô Ozu's Japanese masterpiece "Tokyo Story." You'll want to immediately pick up the phone, call your grandparents and tell them how much you love them.
reviews.author: Jason Fraley

reviews.text: Injecting what is a tragic setup with comic elements requires a precarious balancing act from the filmmaker and star alike, but Wang and Awkwafina traverse the tightrope without a wobble.
reviews.author: Prahlad Srihari

reviews.text: The Farewell becomes a gentle, universal plea that showcases all the perks and drawbacks of having a family.
reviews.author: Shikhar Verma

reviews.text: A poignant look at cultural identity and its place in modern society.
reviews.author: Wesley Lovell

reviews.text: The Farewell may be a difficult sit for anyone who has lost a loved one, but it's a worthwhile one as it keenly captures the glorious awfulness and fabulous ridiculousness of family.
reviews.author: Frank J. Avella

reviews.text: What The Farewell isolates so incisively is a sense of cultural melancholia specific to the immigrant experience, a mourning for something lost in the process of existing between worlds.
reviews.author: Isaac Feldberg

reviews.text: So well-acted, you felt it. I thought it was a really, really solid movie, and I was very surprised by it.
reviews.author: Justin Brown

reviews.text: The Farewell is among 2019's best films. It becomes deeper, funnier and more resonant with repeated viewing, too.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: Wang's film simmers on a low flame, which is also the source of its charm and the empathy it stirs.
reviews.author: Uri Klein

reviews.text: This is a humane, wise treasure of a movie.
reviews.author: Stephen Rebello

reviews.text: The Farewell reminds us that callous statements of the "go back to wherever you came from" nature are not only racist but demonstrate a pernicious lack of empathy. Nobody leaves home without a good reason.
reviews.author: Jorge Ignacio Castillo

reviews.text: A fascinating film, very well observed ... highlighting all those contradictions, as we might see them, that I do find myself on occasion disagreeing with, but having no leg to stand on.
reviews.author: James Marsh

reviews.text: For obvious reasons it's a film that is close to the director's heart and while not as funny as it could be, its earnestness just about wins through in the end.
reviews.author: Steven Sheehan

reviews.text: 'The Farewell' is one of the best movies of 2019. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: This intimate tragi-comedy is one of the very best films of 2019.
reviews.author: Grant Watson

reviews.text: Not only well-written, but superbly directed with wonderful (and often understated performances).
reviews.author: Ryan Silberstein

reviews.text: Playing a character who allows endless opportunities to speak her heart pass her by, Awkwafina displays her full heartbreaking range dealing with the worst situation imaginable.
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: ...The Farewell is an equally hilarious and heartbreaking examination of grief, family and tradition.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: [Lulu] Wang positions herself as a director of great maturity... and I really hope she continues to have the opportunity to tell more stories of this level. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emmanuel Báez

reviews.text: Until the closing shot, this is a celebration of Asian actors, traditions, and relationships, never tainted with the need to please multiplex audiences of the west.
reviews.author: Amelia Harvey

reviews.text: The Farewell is certainly dialogue-heavy, but it captures the Wang family dynamic through blocking and movement, as Billi both stands out as a westerner in her former homeland, and gets caught up in the sweep of family rituals and idiosyncrasies.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: The Farewell is a personal, compelling family dramedy, but the film goes beyond its premise and genre conventions - carefully unpacking questions about the division between cultural value systems and ways of thinking.
reviews.author: Debbie Zhou

reviews.text: Shoulders hunched, head slung forward, and a look of deep, determined bereavement on her face, Awkwafina makes Billi's grief a palpable force, and it renders the final seconds of The Farewell intensely touching.
reviews.author: M.V. Moorhead

reviews.text: What follows is a series of hackneyed scenes about the different interpersonal relationships within the family, centering on the heroine's bond with her grandmother.
reviews.author: Ben Sachs

reviews.text: You've probably never heard of Shuzhen Zhao who brings Nai Nai to life, but she will create a lasting memory in this role. She's spunky, smart, trusting, and above all, loving, exactly what the term "grandma" means.
reviews.author: Pamela Powell

reviews.text: Thematically, The Farewell is about reconciliation with the past and wrestling with cultural traditions that now seem foreign in a country that once was home. But it's also simply about grappling with loss...
reviews.author: Esther Zuckerman

reviews.text: After watching The Farewell, I found myself sad for no reason, and angry at the movie's happy ending.
reviews.author: Neal Pollack

reviews.text: It's a redefining role that hopefully should be richly rewarded in the upcoming awards season.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: Touching, vulnerable and heartbreaking, Awkwafina enters the world of drama with great confidence and comes away with a performance that should be remembered at year's end.
reviews.author: Bruce R. Miller

reviews.text: I kept waiting for something to happen in the plot of the movie - and then it was over. Oh yes, Awkwafina was very good.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: A marvelous exploration of family and getting a jump on the grieving process.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: Written and directed by Lulu Wang, The Farewell plays out around dinner tables like an Ira Sachs family drama with a cutting, deadpan sense of humor.
reviews.author: Chris McCoy

reviews.text: An extraordinarily gentle drama that is thought-provoking in the nicest, most pleasant way.
reviews.author: Asia Frey

reviews.text: In just 100 minutes of screen time, Wang has brought a contentious, ethical issue to a human level and wrapped it with heart.
reviews.author: Diana Cheng

reviews.text: It's a very rewarding film assembled with a disarming touch of brilliance.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: 'The Farewell' is a rewarding film for the ages. It has its tears, undoubtedly; but it also has many laughs and uplifting moments to carry you through your own obstacles.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: The whole cast is perfect. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: José Martín

reviews.text: The Farewell ends up being an interesting reflection about lies. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Javier Ocaña

reviews.text: Wang moves with discretion between simplicity and eccentricity, addressing solemn themes without any artificiality. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: María Caballero

reviews.text: Like its characters, the movie stays a fair distance from the drama and says it all in silence. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Daniel de Partearroyo

reviews.text: And ultimately, even though this wonderfully character-driven comedy is about death, every second of it is filled with glorious, laudable life.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: There are silences in Lulu Wang's The Farewell that linger much longer than they should and much longer than it is comfortable.
reviews.author: Pim Wangtechawat

reviews.text: The Farewell is a comedy of warmth and bracing honesty. Simply put, it's one of the best films of the year.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: There are big, tear-jerking scenes, with Awkwafina and older actress Zhao nailing the chemistry as to what brings them together, and why saying goodbye will bring such terrible sorrow.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: To see [Awkwafina] shed tears, to watch her struggle with internal conflicts and to hear her deliver everything in Mandarin, she deserves much credit for daring to step out of her comfort zone.
reviews.author: Joanne Soh

reviews.text: What I love most about this movie is that it's the first film since The Joy Luck Club that touches on the collision of Western values and Confucian values... It's such a wonderful film in every conceivable way.
reviews.author: Wade Major

reviews.text: The Farewell can feel careful and overscripted, indicating Wang's personal instinct to protect the characters and not delve too deeply into harsh truths. But this decision feels as loving as the film does.
reviews.author: Roe McDermott

reviews.text: Given how many Americans can claim some kind of migrant heritage, it's perhaps strange there haven't been more films like Lulu Wang's carefully crafted drama...
reviews.author: Jason Di Rosso

reviews.text: Magnificent screen presence. I thought it was really lovely. I thought it was really funny. I thought it was really moving. You will laugh, you will cry.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: Funny, surprising, and poignant in all the right places, The Farewell is the kind of film you will be glad to say hello to.
reviews.author: Alison Rowat

reviews.text: While the film plays with issues of old-world values and modern sensibilities, Wang never seems to be pushing a message. She's simply telling a story from her experience that has universal ramifications
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: It is heartfelt and beautifully observed, so while everyone on screen is doing their utmost to hold back tears, yours will come unchecked.
reviews.author: Jamie Graham

reviews.text: Thoroughly entertaining, this is a farewell well worth saying hello to.
reviews.author: David Aldridge

reviews.text: Zhao Shuzhen is excellent as Nai Nai but Awkwafina is decidedly ordinary.
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: [A] softly observed comedy of familial errors that should appeal to anyone whose family ever sat on a lie, which is to say nearly everybody.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: Armed with a tender, naturalistic screenplay and a charming, committed ensemble, The Farewell is a wonderfully acted family drama, and a note-perfect one, at that. Lovely stuff, altogether.
reviews.author: Chris Wasser

reviews.text: It's wonderful stuff from start to finish, and one of the best films I've seen so far this year.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: Ultimately, it's all about balance, a yin and yang of roots and identities, humour and pathos that comes together into a satisfying, bittersweet wedding banquet of a movie.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: The play between suppression and sentimentality is as engrossing as that between East and West.
reviews.author: Nick Hasted

reviews.text: You'll be spewing with tears before the first act is done.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: In the lead, Awkwafina delivers a wonderfully complex, deeply felt performance that perfectly conveys the maddening nature of family life.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: This film isn't about cancer, it's about the sacrifices we make for family and how we approach mortality.
reviews.author: Jamie East

reviews.text: This apparent simplicity also contains emotional depth. Each frame of the family in The Farewell carries heaviness and lightness at once, indicative of the pain hidden behind everybody's performative happiness.
reviews.author: Rebecca Liu

reviews.text: [A] compelling, spiky exploration of familial duty and cultural heritage.
reviews.author: Daniel Green

reviews.text: One of the most authentic, beautiful movies of the year complete with outstanding performances and a perfectly-honed script.
reviews.author: Brian Gill

reviews.text: A lovely, warm family picture featuring a star-making turn from Awkwafina.
reviews.author: Tara Brady

reviews.text: thoughtful, funny and well observed
reviews.author: Chris Hunneysett

reviews.text: Made with the necessary narrative and directorial guile to get the Oscars in its sights, and with dialogue in English and Mandarin Chinese, The Farewell presses all the right buttons and is a heart-warming tale about cultural dislocation.
reviews.author: Paddy Kehoe

reviews.text: Awkwafina is a joy, as always. The script is smart, and the wedding hijinks give it an obvious structure.
reviews.author: Eve Tushnet

reviews.text: It's a rare film that has the power to make you laugh, cry, and laugh again as deftly as this does.
reviews.author: Mark Harrison

reviews.text: Wang's family story is modestly affecting and deserves an audience, but if it does prompt thoughts about weighing up the importance of emotional truth, they mainly come afterwards.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: There are no grand declarations or tear-stained confrontations, as it's not Downton, mercifully. And if you think grandma knows the truth and is fooling everybody else, you will need to think again, as it's just not clichéd in this way.
reviews.author: Deborah Ross

reviews.text: Panic and self-doubt are at the heart of [the] movie...
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: The film could have had wit, attitude, poignancy, style - or any single one of the four. Instead it slithers along, shallow and soapy.
reviews.author: Nigel Andrews

reviews.text: Immigrant in-jokes abound but this isn't a niche film, it's a crowd-pleaser that's been a box-office hit in the US. Not every scene works but it's an enjoyable watch and Awkwafina is a revelation in a central role.
reviews.author: Anna Smith

reviews.text: Goes softly-softly on the Big Themes, but packs an emotional wallop.
reviews.author: Carol Grant

reviews.text: As sweet and affectionate a story as you can get, 'The Farewell' is a heartwarming, funny tale of family, duty and the softest lies we tell one another.
reviews.author: Brian Lloyd

reviews.text: The Farewell is Awkwafina's first leading role and she is truly a revelation, proving she is more than just the comedy sidekick.
reviews.author: Rebecca Lewis

reviews.text: The Farewell is a heartfelt ode to the complexities of family relationships. Lulu Wang has developed into a filmmaker of great merit after only two films, and that is a staggering achievement.
reviews.author: Mark Goodyear

reviews.text: Both a vehicle for Awkwafina's formidable talents and an incredibly charming ensemble piece. If there's any justice, it'll be remembered when it comes to award-scattering season.
reviews.author: Nick De Semlyen

reviews.text: Say hello to one of 2019's best movies.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: Sweet, comforting, heartfelt, and funny, The Farewell is a fantastic piece of work that is an ample showcase for director Wang's filmmaking chops and Awkwafina's acting skills.
reviews.author: Harris Dang

reviews.text: The Farewell celebrates diversity whilst recognising the emotional similarities that connect us.
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: This is an intricately constructed, deeply personal and surprisingly funny story - one of the real highlights of 2019 in cinema
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: [Writer-director Lulu] Wang balances the comedy and the tragedy of the situation with deft assurance.
reviews.author: Vicky Roach

reviews.text: [T]he film is patient, sensitive, remarkably universal in its specificity.
reviews.author: Tom Augustine

reviews.text: "The Farewell" is informative of Chinese customs, very dramatic, and surprisingly very comedic despite the heavy subject matter.
reviews.author: Jason Escamilla

reviews.text: Awkwafina gives an outstanding performance in this film, along with the rest of the cast in this low key Chinese family drama. The drama is also lightened with some comedy.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: A feather-light film whose inconsequential breeziness is perfectly complemented by its brevity.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: There's plenty of humour, especially in the lengthy wedding sequence with its speeches and songs; but the film's main strength lies in its sympathetic examination of the differences between the Chinese who have never left China and their cousins...
reviews.author: David Stratton

reviews.text: Sometimes it is kosher to tell a lie. That's the premise of writer-director Lulu Wang's affectionate story of her own family's ends and means.
reviews.author: Andiee Paviour

reviews.text: Awkwafina is about as far from her role in Crazy Rich Asians as she can be here, and we're with her all the way.
reviews.author: James Bartlett

reviews.text: This exquisite experience is not depressing in the slightest. Conversely, you will leave in a state of hope and happiness most movies could never hope to inspire.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: Immigrants, for whom such experiences often overlap in intimate ways, can tell some of the most compelling stories about the human condition and the dislocating shocks of modernity.
reviews.author: Zoë Hu

reviews.text: Lulu Wang's semi-autobiographical indie charmer The Farewell cuts deep and close to home.
reviews.author: Aaron Yap

reviews.text: Launches no thunderbolts, no dazzling revelations. The film is too gentle for that, with too much affection for its characters.
reviews.author: Sandra Hall

reviews.text: An utterly engaging experience, [Lulu] Wang's film succeeds as both a form of entertainment and an intimate reminder of the importance of family.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: The Farewell is a funny, somber, and thoughtful true story of grief and acceptance. It's one of the best films of the year.
reviews.author: Nicolás Delgadillo

reviews.text: Proof that a diverse workforce leads to better innovation and better products and services.
reviews.author: Frank Wilkins

reviews.text: Awkwafina is our avatar here...you really get to know her, fall in love with her...a lot of this is getting a sense of what life in China is like on the day-to-day.
reviews.author: Martin Thomas

reviews.text: So many well-composed shots. It's a very indie film...but this is a real, feeling film.
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: The clash of cultures and tug-of-war over familial connections to the past eventually comes down to one thing: it's the time you spend with your family that really matters in the end.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: It's gratifying to stumble into a movie operating at the scale of people.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: [The Farewell] is wonderful, and it's one of those rare films that would work for pretty much anyone. Unless you're heartless. Then maybe not.
reviews.author: Marianna Neal

reviews.text: Wang is able to make her own personal culture clash, complex as it is, relatable to American moviegoers - especially to those who still believe in the notion of America being a multicultural melting pot.
reviews.author: Dan Webster

reviews.text: The Farewell is an important exploration of the cultural limbo many Chinese-born Americans find themselves in, but its humor and heart will reach all.
reviews.author: Jennifer Bisset

reviews.text: ...the filmmaker delivers an often excessively subdued drama that contains few wholeheartedly compelling or emotional sequences...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: A remarkable, relatable and poignant drama, The Farewell is stunning in its simplicity with Awkwafina delivering a performance that showcases her talent.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: An authentic look at the cultural divide between two wildly different civilisations, 'The Farewell' is a universal tale that will strike a chord with audiences of any nationality.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: Writer-director Lula Wang's autobiographical drama The Farewell delves into complex realities like family dynamics, cultural differences and terminal illness with elegant simplicity.
reviews.author: Brandy McDonnell

reviews.text: Some might dismiss Lulu Wang's (Posthumous) film as an attempt to cash in on the monster success of Crazy Rich Asians. Nothing could be further from the truth.
reviews.author: Carey-Ann Pawsey

reviews.text: The Farewell reveals a diverse culture of grief alternatives unknown in the West of carrying grief together.
reviews.author: Abygai Pena

reviews.text: I didn't expect such visual delights from cinematographer Anna Franquesa Solano, who peppers the film with truly lovely natural light.
reviews.author: Suzette Smith

reviews.text: Run, don't walk to see this heartwarming and heartbreaking film starring the multi-talented Awkwafina.
reviews.author: Brooke Daugherty

reviews.text: Powerfully subdued and thoughtful, The Farewell is a terrific independent film that will remain among the year's best .
reviews.author: Matt Ward

reviews.text: I was fascinated by The Farewell and by Lulu Wang's judgment-free direction. Her command of tone is highly impressive, and she's made a film about the end of life that's frequently funny and warm.
reviews.author: Tim Brennan

reviews.text: The act of not informing someone about their own health -- particularly when a fatal diagnosis is involved -- is a hot-button issue, and the strength of The Farewell is how it patiently explores both sides of the divide.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: Lulu Wang is a new force in filmmaking and I can't wait to see what she does next. She knows how to elicit laughter and tears through revealing human truths and is not afraid to dig into controversial issues.
reviews.author: Julia Swift

reviews.text: A charming portrait of a family struggle. Beautiful performances and an unexpected--and very welcome--ending.
reviews.author: Chris Stuckmann

reviews.text: I recommend it, [but] ... it unfolded for me as a progression of obvious chords, played repetitively and softly. ... There's a difference between artful subtlety and dullness.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Overstreet

reviews.text: With a sparkling ensemble cast, The Farewell explores questions of individual identity and cultural divides and arrives at the conclusion that we mightn't be so different after all.
reviews.author: Philip Martin

reviews.text: Wang does solid work in providing a range of characters to embody different aspects of the emigrant experience, and looks at the differences between those who left and those who stayed behind in unexpected ways.
reviews.author: M. Faust

reviews.text: Careful but pleasingly odd little film.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: Shao is a heartening grandma with a lot of salt to her... She's a figure anyone would love and grieve for, but it's Awkwafina as a young woman feeling like a stranger in both the East and the West, who keeps this story tantalizingly tense
reviews.author: Richard von Busack

reviews.text: It's an understated, gentle film with low-key comedy matched by an underlying melancholy that is more powerful because of its restraint.
reviews.author: Loren King

reviews.text: The second feature from writer-director Lulu Wang is a quiet, gracefully made examination of the Chinese diaspora, cross-cultural differences, and life and death in an extended family.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: Compassionate, endearing comic drama about inter-generational bonding. Its cinematic success proves that diversity is good business.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Director Lulu Wang based "The Farewell" on her own history and at the very end, she gives us an unexpected and upbeat coda. And like everything else in this unexpected and appealing film, it works.
reviews.author: Eleanor Ringel Cater

reviews.text: It's a necessary film... recreated by great actors. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: It is truly hard to say goodbye, especially when you know the end is not some far-off point along the horizon, but close enough to cross in a step or two.
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: But behind the forced smiles, this is a family grieving in advance. The director Lulu Wang doesn't resolve every moment but rather lets it breathe as we watch the family working through their feelings.
reviews.author: Eli Glasner

reviews.text: In its unflappably honest depiction of coming to terms with death, this powerful and often delightful film becomes the most life-affirming seen I've seen this year. It's a keeper.
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: Paradoxically both highly personal yet fairly universal - a remarkable achievement.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: A warm, heartfelt, and often funny story about the bonds of family and the ways we work to stretch them as far as we can; across continents if we have to.
reviews.author: Adam Lubitow

reviews.text: "Farewell" tugs at the heartstrings in many funny, bittersweet, touching ways.
reviews.author: Barry Paris

reviews.text: The Farewell finds the laughs between the tears, with the tone never forced. It's a film that has stayed with me long after I left the theater.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: It's a joyously odd affair that will remind some of 'The Wedding Banquet,' and nicely serves to fill in the blanks among tender moments, a few playful ones, and the universal recognition of love, people and events no matter what language you speak.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: "The Farewell" evokes some of the same emotions as well, making it a generational crowd-pleaser perfect for adult children and their parents to enjoy together. And with their grandparents, of course.
reviews.author: Michael Smith

reviews.text: Movies don't get much more personal than this.
reviews.author: Brad Keefe

reviews.text: Heartfelt and sweet.
reviews.author: Evan Dossey

reviews.text: The Farewell is a movie of dichotomies - Chinese culture and American culture, parents and children, mourning and celebrating, youth and old age - that appropriately straddles the line between drama and comedy.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: [The Farewell] presents us with the struggle to find a more human and fulfilling story in 2019.
reviews.author: Nguyên Lê

reviews.text: The Farewell hits universal themes of kinship and mortality with unerring accuracy and delicate grace.
reviews.author: Robert W. Butler

reviews.text: The movie is a natural tearjerker, given the intense tenderness of the subject.
reviews.author: Hannah Lynn

reviews.text: Rogert Ebert once described the movies as "a machine that generates empathy." The Farewell lovingly lives into that metaphor.
reviews.author: Abby Olcese

reviews.text: Almost every shot, most of them wide, encompasses the entire family and its myriad facial expressions. There's an emotional choreography to this film.
reviews.author: Sadaf Ahsan

reviews.text: Writer-director Lulu Wang knows exactly how to keep every element of her exceptional movie - drama, comedy, emotions, secrecy, and familial love - perfectly balanced. The dialogue is always crisp and the occasional slapstick is flawless.
reviews.author: Michael Calleri

reviews.text: Wang crafts the kind of film you hate to let go of when you leave the theatre, wishing you could stay in the weight of its affections and its grace.
reviews.author: Chris Feil

reviews.text: The Farewell began as a entry in This American Life, and it might have fit pretty well there, in a tight space with words as the prevailing medium. It just does not stretch well to an hour and 40 minutes on a big screen.
reviews.author: Martha K. Baker

reviews.text: The real star is Shuzhen Zhao, who plays the grandmother. Her Nai Nai is a blend of indomitability, charm, shrewdness, and puckish delight.
reviews.author: April Austin

reviews.text: The setup makes for genuinely amusing light farce, but in their patient observation, Wang and cinematographer Anna Franquesa Solano conjure a heartfelt intimacy with the family...[and] the actors always offer up finely etched emotional truths...
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: Wang goes for a very understated and naturalistic tone throughout most the film, but not a scene is squandered.
reviews.author: Thaddeus McCollum

reviews.text: Awkwafina's leading performance is remarkable; With little dialogue, she evokes Billi's turmoil primarily through her eyes and body language.
reviews.author: Brigid Presecky

reviews.text: Wang is a magician, wringing implacable, momentous emotion out of her shots in a truly remarkable way.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: It's a thought-provoking trio - the American-raised millennial, the immigrant parents straddling two worlds, and the older generation left behind in the old country. It's a dynamic that will resonate with many viewers.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: To watch [everyone's] internal war through their expressions is what makes The Farewell such an unforgettable cinematic treat of resonant catharsis.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: Awkwafina finds her footing as a first-time leading lady, excelling with her emotionally nuanced and vibrant performance in a story about familial love and the gray area one cultivates from straddling different homelands.
reviews.author: Kristen Yoonsoo Kim

reviews.text: Perhaps a little heavy for children, The Farewell is best suited for families with teens. And please take them. It's been a long time since a film made me feel like this.
reviews.author: Tania Lamb

reviews.text: Thanks to Wang's deeply personal direction and Awkwafina's subtly profound performance, The Farewell offers a touching and truly authentic experience.
reviews.author: Sandy Schaefer

reviews.text: Wang weaves a powerful tale about trans-cultural humanism.
reviews.author: Nathanael Hood

reviews.text: (Writer/director Lulu) Wang creates a place we never want to leave. The Farewell is one of the best films of 2019.
reviews.author: Michael Ward

reviews.text: "The Farewell" opens for us a window into the intriguing cultural particularities on the other shore, but in its heart are the universal themes of love, regret, and forgiveness that families everywhere share.
reviews.author: Antonio Sison

reviews.text: The Farewell is a subtle masterpiece about family and friendship, love and loss. Director Lulu Wang has also created something more moving than just about anything I've seen so far this year.
reviews.author: Asher Luberto

reviews.text: Authentically heart-warming. 'The Farewell' is one of the most original films of the summer. Awkwafina proves she has the acting chops to take on complex roles. We can't praise this film enough.
reviews.author: Kaely Monahan

reviews.text: Viewers will ... see aspects of their own family throughout the film, which supports the concept that no matter how different we are from one another, we're really all the same in the grand scheme of things and that humanity has no borders.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: "The Farewell" is packed full of memorable scenes and moments, which [Lulu] Wang ties together with a creative and engaging style that involves everything from the framing of her shots to the quirky music playing in the background.
reviews.author: Josh Terry

reviews.text: An extraordinarily confident debut from Wang.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: This indie charmer shows the 'Crazy Rich Asians' standout can do far more than steal a few scenes.
reviews.author: Christian Toto

reviews.text: The Farewell focuses on a family fractured by emigration but still inescapably a family -- with all the tensions, love, accusations and regrets that go with it.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: A pleasing, witty and mature film.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: A film of sorrowful, unassuming elegance, charming in its cultural specificity but thoughtfully somber in its treatment of that universal inevitability, mortality.
reviews.author: Andrew Wyatt

reviews.text: This smart film deftly mixes comedy and tragedy, and manages to be heartfelt without being cloying or sentimental.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: ...isn't that the best you can ask of a film, for it to be enjoyable and thought-provoking? The Farewell checks both boxes.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: The good lie.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: The cinematic equivalent of comfort food, predictable but filling old favorites guaranteed to hit your laughing-and-crying taste buds.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: "The Farewell" drips with authenticity as it examines - and gives equal weight and respect to - the disparate traditions and values of its two colliding cultures.
reviews.author: Greg Maki

reviews.text: Funny without getting coarse and touching without becoming mawkish...a moving tale of a young woman coming to terms with both her grandmother's mortality and her own uneasy place between two cultures.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Comedy, they say, is tragedy plus time, but in The Farewell, tragedy and comedy occupy the same space at the same time, and get along just fine.
reviews.author: Gary Thompson

reviews.text: The story of a wedding held under trying circumstances might not be the type of film that go can toe-to-toe with "Spider-Man: Far from Home" when it comes to total box-office bucks but its very down-to-earth story proves to be its superpower.
reviews.author: Cary Darling

reviews.text: How The Farewell balances questions about cultural heritage and the morality of honesty is immersive and lovely.
reviews.author: Roxana Hadadi

reviews.text: What Wang constructs is a film that packs an emotional punch one minute and has you laughing the next.
reviews.author: Courtney Small

reviews.text: The Farewell is a gift, a stunning, emotional, and nuanced piece of storytelling that will indeed make you want to call your grandmother afterward.
reviews.author: Mae Abdulbaki

reviews.text: Lulu Wang artfully creates something that's less of an explanation and more of an exploration.
reviews.author: Jon Espino

reviews.text: A universal and heart-warming story about the ties that bind a family. I laughed and cried, and it made me call my grandmother right after the movie ended. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: A funny and profoundly moving film; Awkwafina's performance echoes with an intense understanding of the relationships she's portraying. Take tissues, and book somewhere for dinner straight after - there's a lot of food in this movie.
reviews.author: Sarah Cartland

reviews.text: The Farewell  explores the messiness of grief, secrets and family through the lens of east vs. west cultural differences, striking the best balance between comedy and drama.
reviews.author: Joi Childs

reviews.text: The Farewell is one of the best films of 2019. Heck, it might even be one of the best of the entire decade.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: A powerfully affecting drama about cultural and generational differences and the special relationship between grandmothers and their grandchildren.
reviews.author: Annlee Ellingson

reviews.text: Great characterizations with brilliant writing and an astonishingly accomplished ensemble cast.
reviews.author: Michael Medved

reviews.text: Lots of heavy stuff, to be sure, and there are times when The Farewell delivers powerful emotional blows, and we ache for Billi and what she's going through - in large part because Awkwafina's performance is so raw and authentic and in the moment.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Awkwafina is at another crazy Asian wedding but this one comes from real life truths and lies .
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: Wang is a visionary on the rise.
reviews.author: Annie Banks

reviews.text: Skillfully blending humor and sorrow, [Wang has] made an enjoyable and empathetic film about family, mortality and identity.
reviews.author: Anita Katz

reviews.text: On the plus side, Ms. Wang puts her Panavision lens to impeccable use. You can count the number of closeups on one hand.
reviews.author: Scott Marks

reviews.text: Please say "Hello" to Lulu Wang's soulful movie about family.
reviews.author: Jeff Mitchell

reviews.text: A fascinating, moving examination of Chinese-American assimilation, family, and letting go of dying loved ones- and, it's hilarious.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: Writer/director Lulu Wang's lovely, heartfelt film spotlights family with all its quirks and perks.
reviews.author: Karen Gordon

reviews.text: The Farewell finds a nearly impossible balance of being hilarious while being powerful enough to move any audience to tears. If you ever hear someone saying Hollywood can't make great original stories anymore, show them The Farewell.
reviews.author: Brent Goldman

reviews.text: The Farewell finds beauty in life's small moments, as messy as they may be.
reviews.author: Victor Stiff

reviews.text: The handkerchiefs will be out, yet Wang knows how to keep the tears honestly earned.
reviews.author: Robert Horton

reviews.text: In tackling the complexity of grief and the nature of reconciling with death, The Farewell finds fertile ground for both tragedy and comedy.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: The Farewell is a rare film that can entertain, enlighten and reaffirm our fragile humanity.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: This film is sharply written and beautifully performed. It is a perfect example of the adage that the more specific a story is, the more universal it is.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: These ensemble scenes let Wang's craftsmanship shine, as her cast elevates her smart, witty script to something special.
reviews.author: Lisa Trifone

reviews.text: The Farewell tells the often charming, frequently heartbreaking tale of a family struggling with their aging matriarch's terminal-cancer diagnosis.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: The end result is life-affirming and the average viewer is likely to leave the film feeling uplifted.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Never sentimental, never inauthentic, writer/director Lulu Wang hits all the nerves - she should know - it's her story.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: The deep compassion of The Farewell lifts it above its absurd premise.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: It's a considerable act of narrative and tonal juggling...
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Like her heroine, Wang straddles the fence and argues from either side of it; like her, the movie is profoundly Chinese-American, speaking to both audiences and able to be enjoyed by both.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: Sometimes, the movie argues, it's the things we don't say that prove how much we care. Billi's path to acceptance of this makes The Farewell one of the most heartfelt homecoming films in years.
reviews.author: Matthew Monagle

reviews.text: When each of us contains multitudes, "The Farewell" suggests, home is everywhere, or anywhere we happen to be.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: It's a searching picture, not a spongy one, with Wang impressively detailing culture shock with a cast of capable performers.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Lulu Wang's sophomore directorial work is one I can readily describe as masterful. Awkwafina is simply tremendous & mesmerizing. I sure hope the Academy won't overlook this superb film next year.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: Wang [suggests] that how one feels about families telling the truth--whether they must be forthright with one another at all times--depends on the culture they have been immersed in.
reviews.author: Phil Guie

reviews.text: "The Farewell" is an unexpected movie because of its overall direction.
reviews.author: Samantha Incorvaia

reviews.text: It's immensely entertaining to watch.
reviews.author: Ken Eisner

reviews.text: Lulu Wang's semi-autobiographical film will make you laugh and cry. Awkwafina's natural intensity is a dynamic match for Shuzhen Zhao's energetic performance. The best film of 2019.
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: The Farewell is a more substantive, engrossing and ultimately deeper work about the bonds that hold and strengthen us.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: Drawing from a deeply personal story, director Lulu Wang’s sophomore feature film shines comedy into drama on a culturally unique situation of gallows humor.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: While Wang may stint occasionally on the sort of character detail separating a very good film from a great one, "The Farewell" takes you to a humanely eccentric place.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: The Farewell has a power, grace, and perceptiveness that reaches beyond its own unique cultural specificity.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: It has an eye for absurdity and for the telling detail, and it marks Lulu Wang as a director with the rare but essential ability to make you care about what she cares about.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: Awkwafina shines in excellent dramedy about family, culture.
reviews.author: Tara McNamara

reviews.text: It's naturalistic without feeling downbeat, farcical without being goofy, and treats its cultural signposts with a sensitivity and honesty few filmmakers can achieve.
reviews.author: Clint Worthington

reviews.text: This is a sweet, emotional journey of love and respect for family and Awkwafina's breakout leading role showing the comedian/rapper's dramatic versatility.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: There are moments of recognition in some of the even more infuriating scenes that made me laugh through reluctant tears.
reviews.author: Megan Reynolds

reviews.text: It's a film that pulls off a quiet miracle: it breaks your heart, and leaves you happy.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: The Farewell is a funny, finely observed generational study about identity, family and obligation, and how all three of those things can be one and the same.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: The Farewell is the ultimate "fly on the wall" scenario
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: The Farewell leaves you marveling at sincerity, selflessness, and grace, and nursing a need to call your grandmother.
reviews.author: Soraya Nadia McDonald

reviews.text: There were choices that could have made "The Farewell" into just another feel-good comedy or overwrought drama, but [Lulu] Wang is such a gifted writer and filmmaker that she knows how to make a story both enveloping and subtle.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: Lulu Wang is a triumph of the will... [as] The Farewell invites, delivers, cultural appreciation.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: A heartfelt look at culture and family traditions no other film has captured such depth.
reviews.author: Sarah Knight Adamson

reviews.text: The Farewell feels like a cathartic piece of cinema.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: Wang masterfully navigates this story and all the complicated nuances that go along with it.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: Rarely has a film about death been as life-affirming as this powerfully heartfelt drama that finds the right balance of humor and heartbreak.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: [T]he movie is compact, coolly heartwarming, and gratifyingly uncute.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: Lulu Wang's  The Farewell  is a heartfelt look at culture, identity, tradition and saying goodbye.
reviews.author: Jazz Tangcay

reviews.text: The Farewell wasn't the tearjerker I craved. But by weaving a story of life, death, lies, and love, it gave me a comfort I hadn't expected, yet needed and treasure.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: The Farewell dares to venture to the last chapter of our existence as it examines how an Asian family handles the finish-line process. It does so with a warm-hearted and uplifting spirit that is quite affecting.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: [A] gorgeous movie about universal themes of grief, loss, family, and identity.
reviews.author: Kevin Fallon

reviews.text: The Farewell says a whole lot about grief, guilt and determining what's important in life, while still providing its share of laughs.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: This is a purposeful and crowd-pleasing film that never hits any of its points too hard, because [Lulu] Wang has too much to cover to let any one message drown out the others.
reviews.author: Noel Murray

reviews.text: This goodbye is complicated. That's what makes it work so well...Lulu Wang has made a film so deeply personal we have no choice but to recognize her story as our own.
reviews.author: Sherin Nicole

reviews.text: The Farewell is a remarkable, powerful achievement.
reviews.author: Todd Gilchrist

reviews.text: One of the finest family comedy-dramas to come along in some time.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: The action might take place largely in a distant country, but there's nothing foreign about the emotions.
reviews.author: Thelma Adams

reviews.text: The film taps into universal truths about the passage of time, the inevitability of loss, and how we prepare one another for it.
reviews.author: Pat Brown

reviews.text: ...stays true to the sadness of its central premise.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: On screen, Awkwafina can feel more like a personality than an actress; still, she finds something appealingly honest and vulnerable in Billi.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: The Farewell makes it hard to say goodbye.
reviews.author: Inkoo Kang

reviews.text: For her second feature, up-and-coming writer-director Lulu Wang has drawn on her own experiences to craft a touching story of a Chinese family. The Farewelltakes its time unfolding but pays off in a deeply moving conclusion.
reviews.author: Leonard Maltin

reviews.text: The Farewell crackles most when Awkwafina and Shuzhen are on screen together, in scenes both happy and sad. Their chemistry is nothing short of perfect, rendering the dramatic irony of the story devastating.
reviews.author: Matthew Dougherty

reviews.text: The Farewell is not designed to send you back out into the world feeling that you've learned or accomplished something but rather that you've only just begun a new relationship with life and death.
reviews.author: David Bax

reviews.text: The lovely paradox of The Farewell is that everyone in it tries to hide their feelings as long as they can, yet their story goes straight to your heart.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: The Farewell is a rare and rewarding gem, a movie that trades in pauses and silences and understands that it's the space in between that so often defines our lives.
reviews.author: Robert Levin

reviews.text: The Farewell [is] a vivid and endlessly relatable story of fractured identity in a globalized world.
reviews.author: Manuela Lazic

reviews.text: "The Farewell" is a stoic and honest representation of a flawed and lovely family coming to terms with the inevitable.
reviews.author: Lindsey Bahr

reviews.text: Extraordinary on every level, Lulu Wang's The Farewell starring an award-caliber Awkwafina builds a funny, touching and vital film about what makes a family in any culture, leaving you with cathartic tears.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Wang distinguishes herself as a thrilling new voice in filmmaking by crafting one of the most sensitively told stories of the year.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: I came out of seeing "The Farewell" and my thought was "That was my Nana!"
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: "The Farewell" unfurls a bittersweet emotional journey buoyed by the complicated matter of identity that confronts many immigrants and first-gens when returning "home."
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: Wang turns her frustration and bewilderment into a gentle exploration of the cultural differences and generational schisms that have, over the years, opened up within Nai Nai's extended family.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: ...a funny, moving story about the secrets families keep to protect each other.
reviews.author: Marisa Carpico

reviews.text: Awkwafina is a true revelation in "The Farewell." There's a ton of heart on display throughout the film, anchored by her star making turn.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: What makes The Farewell so unbelievably moving is that, through that very specificity, it touches on fundamentally universal themes.
reviews.author: Anne Cohen

reviews.text: It's not always easy to create a story that is both acutely and culturally specific while also being thematically universal. Often, adherence to one over the other loses the nuances of both. It's to Wang's credit that her highwire act is a triumph.
reviews.author: Erik Anderson

reviews.text: With impeccable craft, Wang has created a funny, heartfelt and bittersweet film that will ring riotously true for anyone who knows the joys and agonies of a large, complicated family, regardless of culture, ethnicity or nationality.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: A film that movingly shows the importance of taking advantage of fleeting chances and closing windows is itself the rarest of opportunities.
reviews.author: Oliver Jones

reviews.text: Wang's film is a must-see, and I'd be shocked if Awkwafina wasn't in the Oscar discussions by year's end.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: You can read that it comes from a personal and passionate place, and the real deep thought about what it all means is palpable as the philosophical questions get deeper and deeper.
reviews.author: Eric Eisenberg

reviews.text: [The Farewell] is a finely tuned drama that finds humor in the everyday absurdity that comes from belonging to a family.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: Funny, melancholic, warm, sweet and poignant all at the same time. In other words, it's like life itself. Awkwafina should be nominated for Best Actress. It deserves to become a sleeper hit.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: A crushingly bittersweet mood dominates the film, and Wang demonstrates a steady hand in her balancing of morbid material and warm, culturally insightful humor, threaded together by a minimal, sentimental score of dulcet vocals and a single violin.
reviews.author: Beatrice Loayza

reviews.text: Unfolds an intriguing charade that will make you wonder whether white lies are perfectly acceptable.
reviews.author: Harvey S. Karten

reviews.text: Wang excels with this mixture of levity and heart tugs, personified in Mr. Li, Nai Nai's dismissively treated live-in boyfriend who shuffles about like a ghost, attending to her needs.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: Though best known for playing wacky comedic side characters, here Awkwafina gives a grounded soulful performance that's both funny and three-dimensional.
reviews.author: Orla Smith

reviews.text: The Farewell has understandably become one of the most beloved films on this year's festival circuit - and one that I'm afraid to say left me cold, despite the strength of Wang's direction and the understated performances by the entire ensemble.
reviews.author: Alistair Ryder

reviews.text: Deftly balancing heart and humour, The Farewell is a success on all counts.
reviews.author: Joni Blyth

reviews.text: A consistently entertaining family drama that is culturally perceptive while maintaining a broad enough appeal that it stands as an undeniable, crowd-pleasing hit.
reviews.author: Tom Beasley

reviews.text: The Farewell exhibits a well-balanced combination of humor and sorrow, of family gatherings with plenteous food, joy, and old animosities that ebb and flow and sometimes pass by the younger generation.
reviews.author: Lauren Humphries-Brooks

reviews.text: The Farewell is a perceptive examination of family bonds, generational differences and cultural contrasts.
reviews.author: Adam Sweeting

reviews.text: The Farewell really resonates when it comes to the overwhelming experience of returning to the motherland, with lingering shots of changing neighbourhoods, and childhood memories floating to the surface.
reviews.author: Katherine McLaughlin

reviews.text: The Farewell is a humane and moving look at the cultural differences between East and West and the difficulty of finding a way of reconciling them when you have grown up as an immigrant in another country.
reviews.author: Alexa Dalby

reviews.text: Lulu Wang successfully marries comedic talent with sensitive writing to universalise her experience.
reviews.author: Ella Kemp

reviews.text: The Farewell is an overwhelming tragicomedy that hits you with a sledgehammer punch of emotions.
reviews.author: Ben Rolph

reviews.text: A rare family film that genuinely speaks to the deep, historied, and complicated bonds that tie while remaining thematically viable and content appropriate for practically all ages.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: Writer/director Lulu Wang deserves a great deal of credit for the sensitive, touching, and frequently funny dramatization of an event that's clearly quite personal for her.
reviews.author: Audrey Fox

reviews.text: The Farewell is a tragic story that brings absolute joy.
reviews.author: Rosalie Kicks

reviews.text: Please keep giving Lulu Wang money to make movies.
reviews.author: Luke Hicks

reviews.text: What results is a masterfully executed and earnestly-felt look at a complicated and painful situation for this family.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: It unearths the universality of complex familial love that defies borders and language barriers.
reviews.author: Tomris Laffly

reviews.text: Lulu Wang's film sympathetic film goes far beyond showing the cultural clash between the family. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ana Laura Pérez Flores

reviews.text: "The Farewell" is not a film about loss or grief. It is about family and identity and love. It is about the people we are and how we become.
reviews.author: Karen M. Peterson

reviews.text: The Farewell has some beautiful, truthful things to say about how love persists across the oceans.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: Like early Ang Lee ... writer-director Lulu Wang weaves humor, discomfort, tragedy, and introspection into her story of inevitable loss. [The Farewell is] a familial masterpiece
reviews.author: Matt Patches

reviews.text: A breakout role for a star on the rise, The Farewell goes well beyond its simple narrative and presents us with something profound and entertaining at the same time.
reviews.author: Jason Gorber

reviews.text: The Farewell dives straight into the deep end with authentic representation, handily revealing the infinite diversity within Chinese identity alone.
reviews.author: Li Lai

reviews.text: The Farewell is crazy good and so is Awkwafina, who is having one hell of a joy ride. This doll has flipped the script turning in a very heartfelt dramatic performance that will break your heart.
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: Bittersweet, touching and always funny, The Farewell is lived-in from top to toe.
reviews.author: Dan Mecca

reviews.text: Awkwafina is amazing in everything, but she's especially good here in a lead role.
reviews.author: Evan Saathoff

reviews.text: A bittersweet look at a young woman contending with her Chinese family's many generational conflicts.
reviews.author: Eric Kohn

reviews.text: The Farewell stands as proof she's capable of much, much more. Awkwafina shoulders this dramatic leading role with the grace, and a showstopper monologue near the end of the film should win over any final skeptics.
reviews.author: Angie Han

reviews.text: "The Farewell" is a remarkably cohesive ensemble movie.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: Lulu Wang's script is overflowing with authenticity, honesty, and humor. It portrays a family in a very trying time but never loses itself in being overly sentimental or trite.
reviews.author: Ashley Menzel

reviews.text: Wang's film is a joyous celebration of family that is handled in such a unique way that it is even more effective than the majority of other films that have tackled this subject.
reviews.author: Scott Menzel

reviews.text: [Director Lulu] Wang movingly tells not just a story about the negotiations of familial love, but also of the immigrant experience, of revisiting one's homeland to, in some senses, say goodbye to it.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: There's an avoidance of obvious culture clash comedy... instead Wang deftly details both the guilt of living so far from family and how one's concept of what home really means can get so tangled.
reviews.author: Benjamin Lee

reviews.text: The Farewellis a movie full of unique insights on family and what it means in different parts of the world.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: It's a universal, well-told story any audience will adore.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: The Farewell is wonderfully specific towards the culture depicted, but there's a universality to its issues regarding family. Just about everyone will be able to take something away from The Farewell.
reviews.author: Matthew Passantino

reviews.text: By turning cultural expectations on their head, director Lulu Wang arrives at a sweet, moving, tender story of family bonds.
reviews.author: Matt Goldberg

reviews.text: All the characters are finely observed, as are the relationships between them. The friction and love between in-laws, between generations, and between families with different cultural values is recognizable and true.
reviews.author: Murtada Elfadl

reviews.text: The result is a story that's both culturally specific and emotionally universal, as it gives a talented star a chance to shine.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: In Lulu Wang's lovely, melancholy The Farewell, Awkwafina breaks out in a much bigger way with her first major role, creating a wholly realistic character, and revealing a talent for dramatic acting that you may not have realized she possessed.
reviews.author: Chris Evangelista

reviews.text: The little dramas and themes that emerge during the reunion of the film's far-flung brood become, like a family, more than the sum of its individual parts, and an incredibly satisfying meal of a film.
reviews.author: Emily Yoshida

reviews.text: If the ending doesn't make you tear up than I don't know what to say. There are some pacing problems but all the acting is good and overall I really enjoyed it
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: Wang's The Farewell is an incredible outlook on family tradition that is thought-provoking, relative, and personal. All while providing a stupendous performance by Awkwafina.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: The Farewell's simple manner makes for a knockout of emotional resonance.
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: Wang is a filmmaker to watch, whose serio-comic and delicate sense of the human condition will take her far with audiences.
reviews.author: Anthony Kaufman

reviews.text: A warmly satisfying family affair.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: What makes "The Farewell" so effective is that in delving into such a specific case, the film invites audiences to reflect on the passing of relatives close to them.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

synopsis: Billi's family returns to China under the guise of a fake wedding to stealthily say goodbye to their beloved matriarch -- the only person that doesn't know she only has a few weeks to live.
